title: EPIC: what mimid needs if MIMI interop is mandated (DMA Article 7)
description:
Mark's analysis, 2026-11-22. Beaded out at his instruction. The premise
is not hypothetical: DMA Article 7 already obliges gatekeeper messaging
to interoperate, and that obligation is the lever that would make MIMI
the NAMED protocol rather than each gatekeeper shipping its own spec.

THE ONE-LINE FINDING: the feature list is mostly done. What is missing
is everything that only matters when the peer is not friendly and the
volume is real.

Today mimid has interop-tested against ONE implementation (Haven),
cooperatively, with its author answering email. That is the thing that
does not generalise, and it does not compress: the work is interop
testing.

CAVEAT recorded with the analysis: it is written against protocol-07,
content-10 and room-policy-04. Nobody here knows what a June 2028
document says. The per-ambiguity decision-bead discipline is what makes
retargeting to a final RFC tractable at all, and is worth keeping for
that reason alone.

STRUCTURE. Children of this epic, grouped as Mark grouped them:

Hard blockers (the peer is not friendly, the volume is real)
- follower catch-up: mimid-1wgh.37.104, designed this session. At one
  friendly peer it is a design note; at twenty commercial peers it is a
  daily occurrence, and today the failure is permanent ciphertext loss
  with no notification. This is the one item where the WG work matters
  MORE than the implementation: if it is not in the final spec, every
  provider improvises.
- provider auth a gatekeeper actually accepts: see .1
- ciphersuites including post-quantum: see .2
- multi-device at real volume: mimid-4lp4
- identity past BasicCredential: see .3

Content coverage, the user-facing half, and thinner than the transport
half: see .4

The regulatory surface, where abuse reporting and consent stop being
optional: see .5

Operational, not protocol: discovery past the configured peer map
(mimid-1wgh.37.94), retention as a contract rather than a setting, and
machine-readable refusals (mimid-1wgh.55): see .6

AND THE DECISION THAT COMES FIRST: conformance target or full provider.
See .7. Mark's own push-back is that "plug into all of them" reads as a
feature-completeness problem and is not one; the better position may be
to be the independent implementation that can CHECK whether the
gatekeepers' claims are true. That needs far less of the content list.
The two paths diverge sharply after the hard blockers, so the choice
should be made before the hard blockers are finished, not after.
notes: CORRECTION 2026-11-22: this epic's description framed the role question (mimid-7yn7.1) as a fork that had to be chosen before the hard blockers finished. Mark pushed back -- 'i honestly dont get why both is so expensive' -- and he was right. The conformance capability is already built and already in use: strict decoding, the fixed fixture direction, a decision bead per ambiguity, the findings log, and decision mimid-1wgh.52 item 2, which already has mimid refusing a peer's request and citing the section. The expensive thing is the content list, and it costs the same whether or not mimid is also a referee. mimid-7yn7.1 is closed as a false trade, the block on mimid-7yn7.5 is removed, and the one real cost that survived is now mimid-7yn7.9: publishing findings about others raises the bar on being right, evidenced by four of my own wrong findings about Haven in a single session.
